items.title: Larry Ridley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 10, 2003
items.q: Sonny Rollins man, Wynton Kelly man, all these guys man...

ctx.x: Yes. So he lived in the house, and she’s like my sister you know. And Billy Fraser, Slide Hampton, all of us, Freddie Hubbard, we all lived in that house. And there was so much music and Yusef Lateef and all kinds of people would come through the house. And Coltrane and I used to go out to Coltrane’s house and hang out with him. I knew him man, I knew this guy. And he was so beautiful and so focused. Sonny Rollins man, Wynton Kelly man, all these guys man, Philly Jo Jones took me on like a little brother, taught…

were a lot of critics and historians that I take issue with because they are not of the same mold like the Leonard Feathers or the Dan Morgensterns. They don’t have the same kind of humbleness and the same kind of commitment. Some woman came up to me the other day because she was very disturbed about what Oscar Peterson said at the gala the other day. And she asked me, “What do you think about that?” I said, “He was absolutely on the money.” She said, “What?” I said, “Yes, he was telling you the truth. I mean…

items.title: Larry Ridley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 10, 2003
items.q: But he also gave deference to the Red Garlands, the Tommy Flanagans, the Hank Jones, the Wynton Kellys, Bill Evans, etc.

ctx.x: Well that’s my question. What was the difference?

That’s one of the things that I wish would happen again. See because a lot of what I went through personally, like Clifford Brown and different ones, Horace Silver and all, any of the guys you want to name, Donald Byrd or Barry Harris. Any of us that were coming along, we played with the older musicians. It was an apprentice period that you served. Now there is so much industry involvement of record companies wanting to sign people. And then they sign a lot of young people because many of them, they don’t know…

really. And everybody is rushing to get — now they’re able to make their own CDs. And I was talking with some of the people from WBGO-FM in Newark. And they were saying that every week they get flooded with CDs from people they never even heard of. And they put on some of them and they are terrible. But what can you do? People have access to make them. And I think that the albums I’ve made I put a lot of thought into. And this is one of the things I admired about Herbie Hancock when he started doing his thing.…
